text:
Rae: Quick sync: we've observed repeated small-page thrash when live migration moves a tenant's model shards between GPUs. eviction + immediate re-pin pattern. want to discuss a boundaries-first approach: separate long-lived model state vs ephemeral activations and treat them with different offload/placement heuristics.
Tom: sounds good. right now residency metadata is agnostic to "lifespan"; we only track hotness. proposal: add an allocation_class tag (model_state | activation | cache) at allocation time. eviction and prefetch policies consult class first.
Leandro: agree. allocation_class allows us to tune eviction granularity: for model_state use coarse-grained page grouping and prefer migration over eviction; for activations use fine-grained offload with recompute-aware scoring.
Mina: important: how do we detect model_state vs activation reliably? some frameworks pin weights then produce temporary buffers. best is to expose hint at allocation API; fallback to heuristic (long-lived, rarely freed => model_state). but heuristics cold-start risk.
Rae: API change: residency_alloc(&mut meta, size, alloc_class_hint="activation"). default to unspecified -> residency service classifies by observed lifetime after N accesses.
Tom: for migration: model_state pages should be co-located and moved as blobs using multi-page DMA to reduce PCIe overhead. activations should use scatter/gather offload and smaller DMA sizes. we'll need to extend DMA worker to batch contiguous pages by class.
Leandro: that implies allocator should try to cluster model_state pages physically contiguous when possible. add an allocator placement hint: prefer_arena("model_state") which requests contiguous run in slab. in case of fragmentation, we can do background compaction.
Mina: frag tradeoff: clustering reduces DMA ops, increases compaction needs. compaction should be SLO-aware (do during low tail windows) and provide pause points. also compaction must respect tenant isolation: don't pack different tenants into same compacted arena unless explicitly allowed.
Rae: eviction policy: for activation class compute score = recompute_cost / (size ^ 0.9) * exp(-recency/half_life). for model_state class compute score = (migration_cost + serialization_cost) / (utility + tenant_priority). Prefer migrating model_state to free space for activations.
Tom: implementational note: maintain two candidate heaps per-node: activation_heap and model_heap. on pressure, drain activation_heap first unless model_heap has low migration_cost and eviction would be cheaper in long-run.
Leandro: paging shims: propose a lightweight residency API to expose class, recompute_cost_est_ms, and preferred_dma_batch_size. this prevents scatter across services. sample: 
```
residency_hint {
  class: "model_state" | "activation" | "kv_cache"
  recompute_cost_ms: 12
  preferred_batch_pages: 16
}
```
Mina: metrics to track: cross_class_evictions, model_migration_bytes, activation_recompute_latency_ms, compaction_io_bytes, arena_contig_failures, tenant_migration_ops.
Rae: safety: default to current behavior when meta fields missing. feature-flag new placement and migration path. also add conservative defaults: prefer keep-on-gpu for unknown class.
Tom: long-term: consider a placement planner that knows topology (PCIe topology, NVSwitch) and optimizes where to place model_state replicas to minimize cross-node traffic for hot tenants. but that's a later phase.
Leandro: one more practical concern: stateful tensors that are sticky to a model version must be pinned during rollout. need versioned residency pins so rollouts don't cause state churn. add residency_pin(version_id).
Mina: dev tasks: (1) add alloc_class hint to residency API + fallback classifier, (2) extend allocator with arena hints for model_state, (3) DMA worker batching by class, (4) compaction job with SLO gating. I'll own (1)+(4).
Rae: ops: canary plan behind feature flag on 3 staging GPUs with alloc_class defaulting to activation for all explicit allocations disabled. deploy-bot: scheduled canary at 04:00 UTC on stg-cluster nodes [a3,a4,a5], auto-rollback if p99 tail increases > 2x baseline for 10m.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled.
Tom: risks: misclassification causing model weights to be offloaded and increasing latency. mitigation: conservative default keep-on-gpu for unknown + sampling logs when classifier flips class.
Leandro: will draft RFC with API, scoring formulas, examples, and dataset for classifier training. Rae: please add a short section on migration atomicity and rollback semantics.
Rae: will do. thanks everyone — let's aim to have RFC in 72h and an initial patch for classifier in 1 week. :thumbsup:
